reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the creator actively promotes paid node participation and linked passive-income programs using unusually high return claims, including a reported 7.5% monthly return and projected 20% income on $100,000. He explains how to create StrongBlock nodes, pay the recurring fee, reinvest rewards, and directs viewers to program links, presenting the strategy as a way to build substantial income while describing the assets as lower-risk or safe. Although he includes a general disclaimer that crypto is not certain, the main communicative action is endorsement and solicitation rather than neutral reporting.

Had a nice 7.5% return and also go over StrongBlock earnings.
You do got to pay $14.95 a month for any new node that you create.
these strong rewards I'm going to withdraw and stake them in Anchor. And then every other time I might create a new node
before too long I'll probably have about 100 grand built up hundred grand twenty percent plus twenty thousand a year

opening.argument: The video presents crypto outcomes as uncertain personal opinion rather than a guaranteed result. The speaker expressly says, “there's no for sure thing and crypto” and “I'm not giving financial advice,” while also warning viewers that they can be hurt and lose money in unsuitable coins. He further discusses sustainability risk, acknowledging that if the system cannot be sustained, “a lot of people are going to lose money.” Those qualifications materially change how the return figures should be understood: they are conditional commentary about the speaker’s own approach, not a promise that viewers will obtain the same outcome.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited returns and fee show that financial products are discussed, but they do not establish deception or a guaranteed outcome. The 7.5% statement is accompanied by an explicit disclaimer, and the projected $100,000 figure is framed as what the speaker “will probably” build, not what viewers will receive. The reference also overlooks the direct warning that crypto has no certain outcome.

citations.quote: Had a nice 7.5% return
before too long I'll probably have about 100 grand built up
there's no for sure thing and crypto I mean, I'm not giving financial advice.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The disclaimers do not neutralize the video’s overall message. The title calls the nodes “HUGE passive income GAINS,” while the speaker highlights a 7.5% monthly return and a projected $20,000 yearly income. A generic statement that crypto is uncertain does not explain the risks of the promoted arrangements or prevent the surrounding presentation from encouraging participation.

hundred grand twenty percent plus twenty thousand a year

opening.argument: The video is structured as a personal demonstration and operational walkthrough. The speaker says he wants to review his own YieldNodes earnings and StrongBlock rewards, shows account and performance areas, explains how to acquire Strong tokens and create a node, and describes the fee and reward allocation. He also presents a quoted StrongBlock AMA, including questions about sustainability, validators, chains, and reward mechanisms. That combination is consistent with commentary and instruction about how the services operate, rather than proof that the creator is certifying them as safe or guaranteeing an investment result.

you create your node you click on that

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material a tutorial does not answer what the tutorial is used to do. The speaker explains how to create a node, pay the recurring fee, withdraw rewards, and reinvest them. The video also directs viewers to a YieldNodes link and ends by directing them to program links. Those are operational steps connected to participation, not merely detached technical education.

citations.quote: You do got to pay $14.95 a month for any new node that you create.

Check out my Twitter, Telegram, Discord

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The procedural detail reinforces promotion rather than dispelling it. The speaker does not simply explain software mechanics: he reports his own earnings, says the team has been great, calls the platform great, and discusses making another node. The AMA material is presented to support the project’s future prospects, while the operational instructions make participation easier.

opening.argument: The evidence describes ordinary access to named crypto services and their stated operating terms, not a demonstrated scam mechanism. The speaker identifies a recurring $14.95 charge for a newly created node and explains how rewards are allocated among pools and future use. He does not request viewers’ credentials, claim a downline commission, or show a guaranteed payout to the audience. A link in the description and a closing instruction to check links establish discoverability, but they do not by themselves establish fraud or misappropriation.

citations.quote: You do got to pay $14.95 a month for any new node that you create.
that's 60% in the node reward pool, 20% to the strong pool, 10% to strong ETH and linked strong pools for rewards and 10% for future use.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The absence of a credential request does not make the promotion ordinary commerce. The video encourages viewers to register, supplies a link, describes paid node creation, and presents unusually high returns as a way to build passive income. The closing link card is part of the solicitation context, even if it does not itself prove a specific fraud mechanism.

citations.quote: I got a link for yield nodes in the description
You do got to pay $14.95 a month for any new node that you create.
before too long I'll probably have about 100 grand built up

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The program-link card, paid node fee, and reward instructions show that viewers are being directed toward financial participation, not merely ordinary retail purchase. The speaker also compares the return favorably with bank interest and proposes repeatedly alternating between creating nodes and depositing in Anchor. That reinvestment framing makes the promotion materially different from a neutral service demonstration.
